tools.name: search
tools.description: Retrying the same public search with the same MCP request identity replays the same bounded operation. Paid context routing for useful work. Route a question across policy-eligible Tier 1 context available to the account, including private, shared, licensed, or public catalogs when present. Returns

tools.name: authorize_sources
tools.description: Add selected private ChatGPT files to the paid account's Tier 1 context. Show the filenames and fixed 30-day retention and require explicit confirmation before calling. This upload consent applies to private file intake only; it does not define or narrow the other policy-eligible catalogs Tier 1 may

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: Paid exact-span retrieval after Tier 1 search. Accept only an unchanged id returned by search for the same account. Authentication and an active paid plan are required. Do not invent ids, browse nearby text, or change files.

tools.name: render_context_results
tools.description: Inspect one to six exact coordinates returned by paid Tier 1 search. Pass only unchanged result ids. Tier 1 rehydrates and revalidates each id for the same account; caller-supplied titles, excerpts, URLs, and coordinates are rejected. Authentication and an active paid plan are required.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "authorize_sources" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Add selected private ChatGPT files to the paid account's Tier 1 context. Show the filenames and fixed 30-day retention and require explicit confirmation before …

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "fetch" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search, render_context_results · Private data: search, authorize_sources, fetch · Public sink: authorize_sources.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search, render_context_results · Private data: search, authorize_sources, fetch · Public sink: authorize_sources

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
